question_text:
The following figure shows the entire graph of a relationship.

Does the graph represent a function?
question_type: Multiple Choice Question with Single Answer
backend_description: The image shows a coordinate grid with a straight line with positive slope passing through the origin.
solution: A function is a special type of relationship where each input (x-value) has exactly ONE output (y-value). Think of it like a vending machine: when you press one button, you should get exactly one snack, not two or three!

To check if a graph is a function, we use the Vertical Line Test. Imagine drawing vertical lines (up and down lines) anywhere on the graph. If ANY vertical line touches the graph at MORE THAN ONE point, it's NOT a function. If EVERY vertical line touches the graph at only ONE point (or no points), it IS a function.
The graph shows a straight line with positive slope passing through the origin.
If we draw vertical lines anywhere on this graph, each vertical line will touch the graph at most ONE point. This means each x-value corresponds to exactly one y-value.
Since every vertical line intersects the graph at most once, this graph passes the vertical line test and represents a function.
Answer: A. Yes
